text:
Marta Lopez: Brain dump from this morning's allocator sync: idea for pluggable defrag policies + cooperative tenant tokens so we can tune fairness and minimize cross-node moves. Short thread.
Kenji Saito: Pluggable policies sounds good. What policies do you have in mind?
Marta Lopez: Two starter policies: 
  - conservative: only in-place coalesce + local pool shuffle, never remote moves. Good for high-SLO tenants.
  - aggressive: allow remote migration when cost model says profitable. Good for batch/throughput workloads.
Priya Rao: How do tenants opt into policies? per-tenant config? default global?
Marta Lopez: Per-tenant policy with a global default. Also introduce a lightweight cooperative token: each tenant has N compaction_tokens that runner consumes when moving that tenant's pages. Tokens replenish slowly. That prevents one noisy tenant from getting all the compaction budget.
Evan Brooks: Nice. Tokens avoid hard isolation and give an economic signal. How do tokens interact with retire windows and DMA tails?
Marta Lopez: Tokens only gate migration/remote moves. Retire window is independent: any migrated page enters RETIRING state for retire_epochs (default 1) to cover late DMA completions. Tokens don't affect retire timing.
Zoe Park: Important: implement tokens cheaply. Keep per-tenant counters in control plane, not on hot path. Runner consults token cache snapshot per epoch.
Kenji Saito: Cost model for remote moves? we need to avoid thrash on NVMe/PCIe.
Marta Lopez: Keep linear: cost_move = size_bytes/est_bw + pcie_latency + cpu_copy_cost. Benefit = sampled_faults * avg_fault_cost. Multiply benefit by tenant_priority and tokens factor. Move if benefit*profit_factor*token_factor > cost_move.
Priya Rao: Sampling hotness again? we agreed 1% RNG EMA before. Do we need anything new for pluggable policies?
Zoe Park: No heavy changes. Policy chooses candidate set; hotness filtering still 1% sample -> tiny EMA. Add a policy hook that can score candidates (cheap score) and then runner applies budget/time caps.
Evan Brooks: What about KV cache interactions? evicting objects may increase fault rates if we move memory out.
Marta Lopez: Good call. For pages backing KV cache we prefer in-place compaction and avoid aggressive shuffles. Add a special hint in allocation metadata: alloc_hint={kv_cache:true} so runner treats them as destabilizing if moved.
Kenji Saito: How do we surface metrics and alerts?
Marta Lopez: Metrics to add: compaction_tokens_used_by_tenant, policy_moves_count, retired_pages, retired_ratio, remote_move_latency_hist, header_retry_rate, stolen_pages_count (pages moved without tokens), reclaimed_under_pressure_count. Alert if retired_ratio>0.2 or stolen_pages_count>0.
Priya Rao: Edge case: token starvation for a tenant that needs defrag (lots of small fragments) but has zero tokens. 
Marta Lopez: Add emergency_token_request API: runner can signal the control plane when a tenant's fragmentation cost > threshold. Control plane can temporarily grant tokens based on global budget. We keep emergency grants rare and audited.
Evan Brooks: Rollout plan?
Marta Lopez: Phase 0: tests + sim of token mechanics. Phase 1: lab canary with conservative policy default and tokens per tenant=2. Phase 2: enable aggressive for a few non-critical tenants. Watch p95/p99 token latency, retired_ratio, compaction_tokens_used_by_tenant.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for branch "pluggable-defrag" on lab-cluster-9 (no traffic) :rocket:
Zoe Park: Implementation notes: pack alloc_hint and policy pointers into existing allocation descriptor to avoid hot-path overhead. Token checks are per-epoch snapshot so no per-access overhead.
Kenji Saito: Correctness: still use indirection header (ptr, seq) and retire-list to avoid late DMA stomps. Readers do read-before/read-after check; migrator toggles seq odd->publish->seq++ even.
Priya Rao: One more: telemetry labels for cost model calibration. We should log move_cost_estimate and observed_move_latency so we can tune est_bw and profit_factor.
Marta Lopez: Agreed. I'll draft the RFC addendum with diagrams, token semantics, and control plane API. Volunteers to review?
Evan Brooks: I'll help with perf harness and token sim.
Zoe Park: I'll help with the alloc descriptor packing and metrics hooks.
Kenji Saito: I'll review the cost model and KV hints.
Marta Lopez: Thanks team. Goal: make defrag respectful of tenant SLOs while still allowing opportunistic reclamation for throughput workloads. Will open WIP PR today. :thumbsup:
